g.title: Adjudicacao
g.text: Case 003 — State liability for a fugitive's crime — adjudication

g.class: node argnode rulenode arg-dvpre_q8 layer-lrc standing
g.title: dvpre_q8

a.xlink:title:
dvpre_q8: dvpre_q8: SpecDuty => ¬sc_q6
If the specific duty of custody stands, the third-party-act defence fails: the realized risk is precisely what that duty was intended to prevent.
Also supported by: Concurring opinion
Supported by dvesp_q0: A prisoner under a closed regime is subject to the State's specific duty of custody, rather than its general duty of public security.

g.class: node argnode rulenode arg-q11 layer-lrc standing
g.title: q11

a.xlink:title:
q11: q11: ¬DueMeasures => ¬suca_q3
Without evidence of due precautions by the State, its claim of a third-party act fails.

g.class: node argnode rulenode arg-sc_q6 layer-lrc defeated
g.title: sc_q6

a.xlink:title:
sc_q6: sc_q6: ThirdParty => ¬cf2lrc_q5
If the crime is a third-party act, it breaks the legally relevant causal connection between the omission and the damages.
Also supported by: Dissenting opinion

g.class: edge argedge defeat from-dvpre_q8 to-sc_q6 between-adjudicators
g.title: dvpre_q8->sc_q6

a.xlink:title:
② dvpre_q8 ⇏ sc_q6
Reporting judge, Concurring opinion → Appellant, Dissenting opinion
If the specific duty of custody stands, the third-party-act defence fails: the realized risk is precisely what that duty was intended to prevent.
Outcome: prevails: defeats sc_q6

g.class: node argnode rulenode arg-u_corte layer-lrc standing
g.title: u_corte

a.xlink:title:
u_corte: u_corte: TimeLapse => ¬suca_q3
The court expressly rejects the claim that time alone breaks causation: elapsed time does not by itself establish a superseding third-party act.

g.class: node argnode rulenode arg-suca_q3 layer-lrc defeated
g.title: suca_q3

a.xlink:title:
suca_q3: suca_q3: TimeLapse => ThirdParty
Party claim: after three months, the crime is a third-party act. It prevails in the preliminary phase by dialectical default, with no effective reply, rather than on doctrinal merits.

③ q11 ⇏ suca_q3
Concurring opinion → Appellant
Without evidence of due precautions by the State, its claim of a third-party act fails.
Outcome: prevails: defeats suca_q3

④ u_corte ⇏ suca_q3
Dissenting opinion → Appellant
The court expressly rejects the claim that time alone breaks causation: elapsed time does not by itself establish a superseding third-party act.
Outcome: prevails: defeats suca_q3

g.class: node argnode rulenode arg-suca_q4 layer-lrc standing
g.title: suca_q4

a.xlink:title:
suca_q4: suca_q4: RobHomicide AND TimeLapse AND GangForm => ThirdParty
Ratio decidendi: elapsed time together with subsequent, independent joint action constitutes a third-party act.
Supported by r2: The prisoner's escape led to the robbery-homicide against the victim.

g.class: node argnode rulenode arg-q_reab layer-lrc standing
g.title: q_reab

a.xlink:title:
q_reab: q_reab: TargetPremed AND ImmedSeq => ¬suca_q4
Distinguishing RE 136.247: premeditation against a specific target and an immediate sequence between escape and crime would defeat the characterization as a third-party act.
Inert: the antecedents were never satisfied.

g.class: edge argedge defeat from-q_reab to-suca_q4 between-adjudicators
g.title: q_reab->suca_q4

a.xlink:title:
⑤ q_reab ⇏ suca_q4
Dissenting opinion → Dissenting opinion
Distinguishing RE 136.247: premeditation against a specific target and an immediate sequence between escape and crime would defeat the characterization as a third-party act.
Outcome: inert: TargetPremed, ImmedSeq outside the factual base; no argument

g.class: node argnode rulenode arg-og_q10 layer-lrc standing
g.title: og_q10

a.xlink:title:
og_q10: og_q10: GenOmission => ¬cf2lrc_q5
Generic omission is neither a necessary nor a determining link to the outcome: it does not sustain the presumption of legal relevance.
Supported by og_q9: After elapsed time and the gang's autonomous deliberation, the State's omission is no longer specific to that outcome: it is qualified as generic.

g.class: node argnode rulenode arg-cf2lrc_q5 layer-lrc defeated
g.title: cf2lrc_q5

a.xlink:title:
cf2lrc_q5: cf2lrc_q5: CaFa_StateOmis_Damages => LeReCa_StateOmis_Damages
If the State's omission is a cause in fact of the damages, it is presumed to be a legally relevant cause.
Also supported by: Reporting judge, Concurring opinion

g.class: edge argedge defeat from-og_q10 to-cf2lrc_q5 between-adjudicators decisive
g.title: og_q10->cf2lrc_q5

a.xlink:title:
⑥ og_q10 ⇏ cf2lrc_q5
Dissenting opinion → Respondent, Reporting judge, Concurring opinion
Generic omission is neither a necessary nor a determining link to the outcome: it does not sustain the presumption of legal relevance.
Outcome: decisive: defeats cf2lrc_q5 without a reply — LeReCa(StateOmis, Damages) leaves the grounded extension

g.class: edge argedge defeat from-sc_q6 to-cf2lrc_q5 between-adjudicators
g.title: sc_q6->cf2lrc_q5

a.xlink:title:
① sc_q6 ⇏ cf2lrc_q5
Appellant, Dissenting opinion → Respondent, Reporting judge, Concurring opinion
If the crime is a third-party act, it breaks the legally relevant causal connection between the omission and the damages.
Outcome: prevails unanswered during argumentation; defeated during decision by ②

The cause-in-fact layer contains no attacks; all controversy concerns legal attribution. Its rules: r0: r0: StateOmis => PrisEscape — Respondent r1: r1: StateOmis AND ClosedReg => PrisEscape — Reporting judge, Concurring opinion, Dissenting opinion r2: r2: PrisEscape => RobHomicide — undisputed r3: r3: RobHomicide => VictimDeath — undisputed r4: r4: VictimDeath => Damages — undisputed
The cause in fact justified in the factual layer enters as an axiom in the antecedent of cf2lrc_q5.
